pages.title: A magazine for the time you spend waiting
pages.lead: Falmouth already gathers in waiting rooms, hotel lobbies, the Chamber, and the library. This magazine is for that time.
paragraphs: Falmouth Wellness Discovery is a quarterly health and wellness magazine with a fold-out discovery map. We print 1,000 copies and place them free. Winter 2027 is the founding issue, and this digital flipbook is a preview of that issue.
The pages follow four pillars: Mind, Body, Soul, and Health & Food. Stories are written from interviews. Open spots are marked as available and link to the partner page.

The printed magazine is letter size, made from 11×17 sheets. Tear out the walking-map sheet: the front is the wellness map, with partner boxes around the edge, and the back is a Falmouth visitor guide. On a wide screen those two sides open as landscape spreads.
Come by Cape Island Café at 316 Gifford Street if you want to talk about a story or a partnership. The phone is (774) 247-5263 and the email is CapeIslandCafe@gmail.com.

pages.title: Where will the new police station go?
pages.dek: Why 100 Brick Kiln Road is in question, and what the Select Board asked for next.
paragraphs: Falmouth planned to build its new police station, and a wastewater lift station for the sewer project, on town land at 100 Brick Kiln Road. An outside legal opinion from the Boston firm Anderson & Kreiger found the parcel is likely protected under Article 97 of the Massachusetts Constitution, because the town used $1.5 million from its Land Bank fund toward the 2003 purchase. Land protected that way cannot be put to another use without meeting legal requirements that include a two-thirds vote of the state Legislature.

On Friday, October 9, the Select Board voted unanimously to release the opinion. Board members said they would prefer town staff to prioritize finding another location for the police station rather than pursue a long effort to clear the restrictions. The town asked its design consultant, Tecton Architects, to update cost estimates for alternative sites and for a one- or two-year delay.

About 35% of the $5.15 million Town Meeting set aside in November 2025 for police station design and project management, roughly $2.58 million, had been spent as of the meeting. Board member Douglas C. Brown noted that much of the architectural work could carry over to another site. Work on the lift station, a separate $16.7 million contract about a quarter complete, was continuing while its legal status is reviewed.

cards.title: What happens next
cards.text: Staff are comparing town-owned and private sites, from flat parcels of about five acres to smaller sites that would need more redesign. Select Board agendas and minutes are posted on falmouthma.gov.

cards.title: Sources
cards.text: The Falmouth Enterprise, “Falmouth Select Board Releases Legal Opinion, Reassesses Police Station And Sewer Project Site,” October 14, 2026 (capenews.net). Status as of mid-October 2026.

pages.title: Good dogs, good neighbors
pages.dek: A volunteer-led shelter partner and a free dog park built by the community.
paragraphs: Since 1990, Friends of Falmouth Dogs has made sure the town's stray and surrendered dogs are rehomed rather than forgotten. Founded by residents who started by walking dogs and raising money, the volunteer-led nonprofit now works with the Town of Falmouth to give every dog in the shelter system daily exercise, enrichment and care, and to match each one with the right family.

The help reaches owners too. Adopters and neighbors describe vouchers for vet care when money was tight, and support for owners during emergencies. Volunteers walk and socialize dogs, foster those who need a calmer place to recover, and help at events.

Once a dog is home, it needs somewhere to run. The Falmouth Dog Park at 257 Brick Kiln Road in East Falmouth is free, handicap-accessible and open from dawn to 8 p.m., with an all-dog area, a small-dog area and a time-out area for nervous newcomers. It is a nonprofit that runs on donations and volunteers, not town money, and it is looking for new board members.
pages.pullquote: A dog park is where a lot of Falmouth neighbors first learn each other's names. Usually the dog's first.
